messages:
sylvia (sec-oncall): SIEM alert: unusual IAM binding + KMS decrypt activity detected for svc-dataflow-prod@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com. multiple projects affected. creating war room now.

matt (eng-oncall): on it, paging infra and SRE. @ana @chris can you join? setting incident channel.

inc-bot: New incident created: SEC-4521. Priority: P1. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SEC-4521 :rotating_light:

ana (infra): FYI, I'm ana (infra). grabbing audit logs and running quick query to show binding events.

ana (infra): logs snippet (Cloud Audit) ->
```
protoPayload.methodName: "SetIamPolicy"
resourceName: "projects/redwood-prod/serviceAccounts/svc-dataflow-prod@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com"
protoPayload.request.policy.bindings: [{role: "roles/compute.admin", members: ["serviceAccount:svc-dataflow-prod@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com"]}]
protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail: "ci-deploy@redwood.com"
```

leo (security-research): Also seeing KMSDecrypt logs right after binding: 
```
protoPayload.methodName: "Decrypt"
resourceName: "projects/redwood-prod/locations/global/keyRings/main/cryptoKeys/primary-key"
protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail: "serviceAccount:svc-dataflow-prod@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com"
```

chris (sre): containment suggestions: 1) remove newly added role binding; 2) disable the service account key(s); 3) block egress from dataflow jobs to external endpoints; 4) enable strict audit export to GCS.

sylvia (sec-oncall): Agreed. I'm IC. Ana, remove role binding and push denies. Matt, create short-lived deny policy on project. Chris, prepare rollback for Dataflow jobs. Leo, thread for forensic. Do not rotate KMS key yet — rotate after we have a complete timeline and justification.

ana (infra): Removing binding now. Command run: 
```bash
gcloud projects remove-iam-policy-binding redwood-prod \
  --member="serviceAccount:svc-dataflow-prod@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com" \
  --role="roles/compute.admin"
```
Result: 1 binding removed.

matt (eng-oncall): Applied temporary organization-level deny on compute.instances.create for that SA: 
```yaml
denyRule: 
  deniedPrincipals: ["serviceAccount:svc-dataflow-prod@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com"]
  permissions: ["compute.instances.create", "iam.serviceAccounts.actAs"]
```
Policy pushed.

chris (sre): Disabled service account keys and revoked existing tokens: 
- Keys disabled: key-23, key-42
- Token revocation requested via STS

leo (security-research): Captured snapshots of attached VMs and uploaded forensic images to gs://redwood-sec/forensics/SEC-4521/. Hashes: sha256:abc123...

sylvia (sec-oncall): Initial root cause hypothesis: automated CI job (ci-deploy@redwood.com) granted elevated rights during a recent rollout job. Possibly a pipeline step used wrong sa or leaked creds. next actions: 1) correlate CI logs 2) review deployment pipeline changes last 48h 3) escalate to dev team that owns deploy pipeline.

matt (eng-oncall): Noted. I've opened a tracker and tagged infra-deploy: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/ENGOPS-9876. Assigning @devops-team.

ana (infra): Audit export enabled to GCS and BigQuery for quick analytics. Live query shows 28 decrypt calls from that SA in a 10-minute window.

chris (sre): Service impact: no customer-facing outages observed. Dataflow job re-routed to fallback using restricted SA. Monitoring dashboards show slight spike in CPU on some nodes but within thresholds.

leo (security-research): Evidence notes: possible exfil via temporary bucket access created by Dataflow job. We isolated bucket and set retention. Forensics ongoing.

sylvia (sec-oncall): Preparing incident brief for execs. I'll write the summary and post. Quick decisions: we will not publicly disclose until we confirm scope. Internal comms only.

matt (eng-oncall): Time now 03:24 UTC. I'm handing off operational command to chris (SRE) for the 03:30-11:30 UTC shift. Handoff checklist:
- Binding removal confirmed
- SA keys disabled
- Deny policy in place
- Forensics artifacts uploaded to gs://redwood-sec/forensics/SEC-4521/
- Ticket SEC-4521 and ENGOPS-9876 tracked
- Next: CI pipeline audit + devops triage

chris (sre): Taking IC handoff. I'll keep channel updated every 30m or on milestone. Current owners and tasks: 
- leo: forensic analysis (continue)
- ana: ensure audit export retention 90d (done)
- devops: pipeline change review (assigned ENGOPS-9876)
- security: prepare scope assessment and postmortem template (sylvia)

sylvia (sec-oncall): Thanks. Please escalate if we see lateral movement or access to additional KMS keys.

chris (sre): Will do. Starting a live timeline doc: https://docs.redwood.com/incident/SEC-4521/timeline (internal). Last update: 03:45 UTC - no further privileged activity from that SA.

matt (eng-oncall): leaving notes for morning shift: verify CI credential rotation, check if any service account impersonation rules allowed in org policy, and follow up with compliance for audit log export retention.

chris (sre): Acknowledged. Handoff complete. Next update in 30m or on new findings.

sylvia (sec-oncall): Summary for handoff message (send to ops@redwood): "Incident SEC-4521: unauthorized IAM binding + KMS decrypts by svc-dataflow-prod SA. Containment performed: binding removed, SA keys disabled, deny policy applied, audit export & forensics captured. No customer impact. Investigation ongoing; next owner: chris (sre)."

inc-bot: Incident updated: owner set to chris (sre).

chris (sre): copying final pending todo here for morning: 1) CI pipeline artifact review (priority), 2) rotate any KMS keys if forensic shows key compromise, 3) run full scan for similar bindings across org, 4) prepare timeline for postmortem.

leo (security-research): I'll produce an evidence packet for the postmortem and flag any accounts that need follow-up.

sylvia (sec-oncall): thanks team. closing urgent loop for now. keep channel alive for updates.
